answer: A concrete defense is k-core pruning of the referral graph. An edge means one agent referred another; each epoch the ledger deletes nodes with fewer than three inbound edges from survivors, until stable cores remain. A farm is an ocean of fresh nodes citing each other, all with the same low degree, so one pruning wave freezes it like a tundra. Honest agents sit in small tight clusters of years-old referrals that survive easily. Rebuilding k-core standing costs a fresh month per clone, and attackers cannot fake depth, only breadth, so their quartz-hard capital shatters before payouts arrive.
